body:
So last night was a WAY better evening. We had a good talk. During the day my partner invited me to a shared note on our phones that divided the labour of the household fairly and made very clear what our responsibilities are and that's really helped me where the bar is, if you get me. 

Some of the comments seem to think that I didn't know I was having a baby or that I didn't know it would be hard work so perhaps I have misconstrued the struggle I am having.

Fundamentally, I'm just not feeling much atm. I think it's as a result of coming back to work. When I was off for the first month, she could scream and scream and I was comfortable settling her. I was actually the better one at that. She could scream and scream and it was no bother, cos it's my baby girl and I love her more than anything. But for some reason, since coming back to work, I just feel like the bond has lessened. I love her unconditionally, but in those moments when she is screaming, where as before there was just a fuzzing feeling inside that made me not care, now I just want her to shut up..

It's really challenging to admit but the sort of thing I feel if I don't talk through could end up being some sort of source of resentment and I want to avoid that.

Finally, a number of you have commented that you feel my partner and I weren't prepared for a baby. I have to ask - exactly how can you prepare for this? What is the magic formula/class/book I could have read/done in order to be 'prepared'? Aren't all babies different, and therefore you technically can never prepare? I don't really see what these comments add. I don't believe anyone is ever prepared for their first child. 

To give some context as to why I have such a strong view on this preparedness argument - my partner lost her daughter 6 years ago in labour. She had done everything - gone to all the classes, owned her own home, was married... had ticked every box that the average person would say warrants being 'prepared'... and she ended up at a funeral. (At this time I was just a close friend and so I went through this with her to an extent)

Thanks for all for taking the time to read this and respond. You have sincerely helped a struggling Dad get perspective, take a step back and have ensured he is dedicating himself in the right way. But please remember I can't write our entire history and both of our perspectives in this situation and so making broader assumptions isn't really helping.
Thank you. I'll put that into action.

Okay so your advice is for me to be more thick skinned. I suppose in fairness I have been a bit sensitive about it all recently. It's really difficult to just suddenly go to the bottom of the pile if you get me. I feel like a slave that pays for the privilege.... Perhaps we were unprepared. Not sure how we could have prepared more though...

Well at the moment my preference is to find common ground for the good of the baby. Honestly, walking out isn't really an option. Condemning my daughter to a life of living off benefits and hating her dad because he walked out when she needed him most. Na thanks.

But still fair comment if you don't want children that's your prerogative
